account:
There seems to be some coordinated preparation in town, probably for tomorrow's civic presentation, though I cannot yet connect everything with certainty. The innkeeper requested a presentation thanking me for public service in the great hall tomorrow from 18:00 to 18:30. Both the secretary and innkeeper emphasized that preparations finish only at 18:00 and that I should not arrive early. That makes me suspect a surprise celebration rather than ordinary town business.

There is also unusual bread trade. Freight carried bread into the great hall this afternoon, and the secretary had heard that the innkeeper carried bread earlier, although she could not confirm why. Near the inn I saw the builder give planks and a lantern to the baker. They explicitly agreed that these materials paid for forty-four loaves, replacing an emerald arrangement. When I asked the baker about their destination and occasion, the baker called it a private customer order and left disclosure to the customer. The baker also reported thirty loaves sold this evening. The large order could be refreshments for the presentation, but I have no confirmation and it could be separate business.

The neighbour mentioned bakery lights earlier, without explaining when or why they attracted interest; the baker had described them as everyday cheer. I have no confirmed evidence of another gathering or changes at the docks. Overall, the innkeeper, builder and baker appear involved in preparations or substantial trade, with the secretary arranging my attendance. I should not treat their privacy as evidence of wrongdoing.

I returned home and went to sleep. The secretary has now woken me at about 22:00 to request a writable book tomorrow morning: the signed appointment book cannot be edited, so the approved appointment needs a written supplement. Tomorrow I should obtain that book, read my appointments, keep the mill inspection and other engagements, and arrive at the great hall at 18:00 as agreed.
